proofs.proof_tex:
For design A, \(\mathrm{lem:design\text{-}a\text{-}fiber\text{-}nonempty\text{-}criterion}\) proves
\[
\mathcal F_A(p,m)\ne\varnothing
\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
m\in\Delta_{\mathcal E}^{\circ}\ \text{ and }\ 
\mathcal C_A(T)\ne\varnothing. \tag{4}
\]
For design B, the onto statement in \(\mathrm{lem:cycle\text{-}to\text{-}scm\text{-}lift}\) gives
\[
\mathcal F_B(p)\ne\varnothing
\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
\mathcal C_B(T)\ne\varnothing. \tag{5}
\]
An empty target set has cardinality zero, so (4)--(5) justify the explicit incompatible-fiber output and show that it is not mislabeled rigid.

On a nonempty fiber, the same lift lemma gives the equalities of target images
\[
\mathcal T_A(p,m)=\{\tau_C(b,a):(b,a)\in\mathcal C_A(T)\},
\qquad
\mathcal T_B(p)=\{\tau_C(b,a):(b,a,m,g,\pi)\in\mathcal C_B(T)\}. \tag{6}
\]
The structural equality and component agreement test proved in \(\mathrm{thm:mixed\text{-}support\text{-}elimination\text{-}complete}\) say exactly that the right side of the relevant equality in (6) is a singleton if and only if all of the compiler's within-component and cross-component tests agree.  This proves both necessary-and-sufficient rigidity assertions.

The same theorem supplies the stated field-relative rational-expression or real-univariate/Thom encoding.  If the target test fails, it supplies two cycle points with distinct \(\tau_C\).  Equation (6) and the cycle-to-SCM lift turn them into legal full SCMs having the same input law and, in design A, the same \(m\).  Finally, \(\mathrm{lem:interior\text{-}cycle\text{-}to\text{-}positive\text{-}scm\text{-}lift}\) proves strict positivity exactly when both selected cycle witnesses are in interior support charts.  This also explains why no positivity conclusion is drawn for cross-face or boundary witnesses.

Let \(R_{\mathrm{SYK}}(p)\) denote the pair given by Appendix equations (A.28)--(A.33) on their regular domain.  By \(\mathrm{lem:shingaki\text{-}yoshida\text{-}kuroki\text{-}regular\text{-}identification}\), every compatible full SCM \(\vartheta\) satisfying their Condition 1 and the observable Conditions 2--3 obeys
\[
\tau(\vartheta)=R_{\mathrm{SYK}}(p). \tag{7}
\]
The compatibility qualification ensures that the full fiber is nonempty, while membership in the present anchor model supplies Condition 1.  Conditions 2--3 and the right side of (7) are observable, so (7) holds for every member of the same compatible fiber.  Hence its target set is the singleton \(\{R_{\mathrm{SYK}}(p)\}\).  The full-rigidity theorem therefore makes \(\mathscr A\) return exactly that value.

For a compatible singular or boundary law, the mixed-support elimination theorem exhausts all rank-one and rank-two modes, inactive endpoints, equal-endpoint split faces, rank-two coefficient faces, and, in design B, all residual forests and the active-cycle condition.  The full-rigidity theorem then returns either the common exact value or two target-changing cycle points, and the cycle-to-SCM lift turns the latter into legal full SCMs.  Equations (4)--(5) in the proof of the full-rigidity theorem show that failure of compatibility is detected before rigidity is assessed.  Thus incompatible inputs are reported separately and are not incorrectly forced into either causal conclusion.

Fix \(\vartheta\in\mathcal F_B(p)\) in the stated no-selection overlap and suppose \(\mathcal K_{\mathrm K}(P_{\vartheta})\).  The cited result \(\mathrm{lem:kawakami\text{-}iv\text{-}proxy\text{-}identification}\) identifies the two conditional response-type vectors \(\omega_0^{\mathrm K}\) and \(\omega_1^{\mathrm K}\) by the simultaneous equations in Kawakami's proof.  In the order \((00,01,10,11)\), response consistency implies that \((X,Y)=(1,1)\) admits exactly types \(01\) and \(11\), whereas \((X,Y)=(0,0)\) admits exactly types \(00\) and \(01\).  Because \(S=1\) almost surely and the selected cells are positive, the probabilities of these two conditioning events are positive.  Therefore
\[
\begin{aligned}
\operatorname{PN}(\vartheta)
 &=\frac{\omega^{\mathrm K}_{1,2}}
         {\omega^{\mathrm K}_{1,2}+\omega^{\mathrm K}_{1,4}},\\
\operatorname{PS}(\vartheta)
 &=\frac{\omega^{\mathrm K}_{0,2}}
         {\omega^{\mathrm K}_{0,1}+\omega^{\mathrm K}_{0,2}}.
\end{aligned}
\]
This is exactly
\[
\tau(\vartheta)=\phi_{\mathrm K}(\omega_0^{\mathrm K},\omega_1^{\mathrm K}). \tag{8}
\]
If \(\mathcal T_B(p)\) is a singleton, it contains \(\tau(\vartheta)\) by definition.  The full-rigidity theorem makes the atlas return its unique element, which equals (8).

It remains to verify the separate scope witness.  Every row of \(A_x^{\mathrm K}(b^{\mathrm{bd}})\) has the form
\[
\bigl(1,b_i^{\mathrm{bd}}(w_1),b_i^{\mathrm{bd}}(w_2),b_i^{\mathrm{bd}}(w_3)\bigr).
\]
Since \(b_i^{\mathrm{bd}}\in\Delta_{\{w_1,w_2,w_3\}}\), the last three entries sum to one.  Thus, for either \(x\), the first column of \(A_x^{\mathrm K}(b^{\mathrm{bd}})\) is the sum of its last three columns, and \(A_x^{\mathrm K}(b^{\mathrm{bd}})\) is singular.  The already established \(\mathrm{thm:experimental\text{-}proxy\text{-}reduction\text{-}and\text{-}boundary\text{-}separation}\) gives
\[
\mathcal F_A(p^{\mathrm{bd}},m^{\mathrm{bd}})\ne\varnothing,
\qquad
\mathcal T_A(p^{\mathrm{bd}},m^{\mathrm{bd}})=\{(1/2,1/2)\}.
\]
Hence the datum is legally classified by the atlas but violates the named invertibility premise of Kawakami's Theorem 1(i).  This proves strict scope separation for this law, without asserting that either theorem subsumes the other.

The local count is elementary.  A nonempty support of one probability vector \(b_i\) has at most \(2^{\ell}-1\) choices, giving \((2^{\ell}-1)^4\) proxy-support products.  On one cell, a rank-two mode has two orientations and, for each \(z\), three coefficient states: left zero, right zero, or both positive.  This gives \(2\cdot3^k\) possibilities.  A rank-one equal-endpoint mode has \(3^k\) split-coordinate faces, while \(\mathrm L\), \(\mathrm R\), and \(\mathrm D\) contribute three further modes.  Summing gives
\[
2\cdot3^k+3^k+3=3^{k+1}+3
\]
per edge, and taking four edges proves the design-A product.  For design B, each of the four response links has either a zero-residual state or an active state with one of \(k-1\) lexicographic pivots and either sign, hence at most \(2k-1\) states.  A relevance witness has one of \(\binom{k}{2}\) pairs and either sign, giving \(k(k-1)\).  Multiplication proves the design-B count.  Endpoint-incidence polynomials not already fixed by a local mode are retained as sign atoms; their sign-invariant subdivisions and the connected components created later are counted in \(B_{k,\ell}\), not silently in the structural-mode product.

Using both incident coefficient vectors gives at most \(4\ell+8k\) endpoint and coefficient coordinates.  Adding projective, margin, response-mass, relevance, and harmless normalization auxiliaries stays below \(N=4\ell+10k+12\).  The table equations are bilinear.  The residual proportionality minors have degree at most four after substitution, and all other support, simplex, normalization, component-scale, cycle-product, and relevance atoms can be kept within degree four by retaining the displayed auxiliaries.  A direct enumeration of the table entries, residual minors, support signs, and normalizations is below
\[
s=100(k\ell+k^2+\ell+1).
\]
These deliberately conservative bounds cover every chart constructed in the mixed-support theorem.

Apply \(\mathrm{lem:effective\text{-}real\text{-}algebraic\text{-}components}\) separately to this finite list.  By definition, \(B_{k,\ell}\) is the maximum of the explicit published output-count and degree bounds at the displayed \((N,s,d)\), together with the structural counts.  It is therefore computable and bounds every component label and real-univariate degree actually returned.  The cited algorithms have at most singly exponential or cylindrical doubly exponential dependence on their finite variable and degree parameters; enlarging constants if necessary gives the stated conservative double-exponential envelope.  This conclusion uses a published effective bound by instantiation, not a new recurrence.

For arbitrary \(\mathbb K_{\zeta}\), all coefficients are obtained from \(\zeta\) by finitely many field operations with divisions guarded by positive margins or recorded nonzero pivots.  The assumed arithmetic, order, sign, and root oracles therefore make every finite call effective.  For rational inputs, clearing those guarded denominators produces integer polynomials.  Instantiating the cited integer bit bounds and real-root isolation bounds defines the computable function \(H_{k,\ell}(L)\), so all coefficients and isolating endpoints have the asserted bounded encoding and the Turing computation terminates.  Finally, the mixed-support theorem proves that component algorithms are called only after the causal structural modes have been exhaustively enumerated and that unequal targets are found by the one-copy refinement (3).  This proves the method restriction.

Let \(H\) be a compact subset of \(\mathfrak R_{\varepsilon}\).  The multinomial central limit and delta result in \(\mathrm{lem:multinomial\text{-}clt\text{-}and\text{-}delta}\), applied to the selected table and to the independent margin table when present, gives uniformly on \(H\)
\[
\sqrt n(\widehat\zeta_n-\zeta)\Rightarrow N(0,\Omega_{\zeta}),
\qquad
\widehat\Omega_n\xrightarrow{P}\Omega_{\zeta}. \tag{9}
\]
The proportional-sample assumption gives the margin block multiplied by \(\lambda\); when margins are known that block is absent.  Compactness and selected-cell positivity make the required second moments and covariance maps uniformly bounded and continuous.

For every incident chart \(\chi\), \(d_{\chi}(\zeta)=0\).  The distance to a closed set is one-Lipschitz, and hence
\[
d_{\chi}(\widehat\zeta_n)
\le \|\widehat\zeta_n-\zeta\|_2
=O_P(n^{-1/2})=o_P(t_n),
\qquad t_n=n^{-1/4}. \tag{10}
\]
Continuity of the finitely many normalized slacks and \(\eta_{\chi}(\zeta)\ge\varepsilon\) imply that the slack test is at least \(\varepsilon/2\) with probability tending to one, uniformly on \(H\).  Conversely, every incompatible chart closure is at distance at least \(\varepsilon\).  The triangle inequality and (9) make its empirical distance exceed \(t_n\) with probability tending to one.  Exhaustiveness of the full atlas ensures that there is no omitted chart.  Thus the selector chooses an incident first-order-compatible chart with probability tending to one.

All incident selected charts have the same value and Jacobian at \(\zeta\), and their extensions have uniformly bounded second derivative on the neighborhoods in the definition of \(\mathfrak R_{\varepsilon}\).  Taylor's formula and (9) therefore give, independently of which qualifying chart is chosen,
\[
\sqrt n(\widehat\tau_n-\tau)
=J_{\chi}(\zeta)\sqrt n(\widehat\zeta_n-\zeta)+o_P(1)
\Rightarrow N(0,V_{\tau}). \tag{11}
\]
Continuity of the derivatives and of the sandwich map gives
\[
\widehat V_n\xrightarrow{P}
J_{\chi}(\zeta)\Omega_{\zeta}J_{\chi}(\zeta)^{\top}=V_{\tau}. \tag{12}
\]
Since \(\lambda_{\min}(V_{\tau})\ge\varepsilon\), (12) implies positive definiteness and hence \(\widehat\gamma_n=1\) with probability tending to one.  Slutsky's lemma applied to (11)--(12) yields the standard normal limit for every nonzero scalar contrast with positive limiting variance and the \(\chi^2_2\) limit for the quadratic form defining the ellipse.  Therefore the corresponding scalar and elliptical Wald regions have asymptotic coverage \(1-\alpha\).

If no chart qualifies, the identities \(\widehat\chi_n=\bot\), \(F_{\bot}=(0,0)\), \(J_{\bot}=0\), \(\widehat V_n=I_2\), and \(W_n=[0,1]^2\) follow directly from the definitions.  The proof above used certification and separation and therefore makes no covariance or Wald assertion for that fallback event.

Write \(q_0\) for the true observable law, including the independent margin law in design A when it is estimated, and put \(t_0=\tau(\vartheta)\).  Each selected-table count has a binomial marginal distribution, as does each margin count.  Exact inversion of its two binomial tails gives its Clopper--Pearson interval the allocated marginal coverage.  The stated Bonferroni allocation over the finitely many cells and both samples therefore gives
\[
P_{q_0}\{q_0\notin C_n\}\le\beta_n. \tag{13}
\]

For a fixed compatible pair \((q,t)\), define the exact upper-tail value
\[
G_{q,t}=P_q\{\Delta_n^{\mathrm{rep}}(t)
                 \ge\Delta_n^{\mathrm{obs}}(t)\}.
\]
This nonrandomized discrete tail value is super-uniform.  Indeed, for any \(u\in[0,1]\), order the finite support of \(\Delta_n(t)\) increasingly and let \(d\) be the smallest support point whose upper-tail probability is at most \(u\), if such a point exists.  Then
\[
\{G_{q,t}\le u\}\subseteq\{\Delta_n^{\mathrm{obs}}(t)\ge d\},
\]
whose probability is the upper tail at \(d\) and is at most \(u\).  Thus
\[
P_q\{G_{q,t}\le u\}\le u. \tag{14}
\]

By compatibility, \(t_0\in\mathcal T(q_0)\).  On \(\{q_0\in C_n\}\), the supremum defining \(\operatorname{pv}_n(t_0)\) includes \(q_0\), and consequently
\[
\operatorname{pv}_n(t_0)
\ge\min\{1,\beta_n+G_{q_0,t_0}\}. \tag{15}
\]
Because \(\beta_n\le\alpha/2<\alpha\), equations (13)--(15) imply
\[
\begin{aligned}
P_{q_0}\{t_0\notin K_n\}
&\le P_{q_0}\{q_0\notin C_n\}
 +P_{q_0}\{G_{q_0,t_0}\le\alpha-\beta_n\}\\
&\le\beta_n+(\alpha-\beta_n)=\alpha.
\end{aligned} \tag{16}
\]
This argument is finite-sample and pointwise at every law.  Applying it at each member of an arbitrary triangular sequence proves the transition claim without a rank or support limit assumption.

We now prove, rather than cite, the optional Hausdorff comparison under the stated local saturation.  Fix one of its compact subsets.  Compactness, selected-cell positivity, the fixed neighborhood radius, and the lower eigenvalue bound imply uniform positive lower bounds for all multinomial probabilities used locally and for \(\lambda_{\min}(V_{\tau})\).  The simultaneous Clopper--Pearson widths with \(\beta_n=n^{-2}\) eventually satisfy
\[
\sup_{q\in C_n}\|q-q_0\|_2
=O_P\!\left(\sqrt{\frac{\log n}{n}}\right)=o_P(1) \tag{17}
\]
uniformly on the compact set.  To see this without an additional limit theorem, for a binomial proportion and \(x>p\), exponential Markov inequality with
\[
\theta=\log\frac{x(1-p)}{p(1-x)}
\]
gives
\[
P_p(\widehat p\ge x)\le
\exp\{-nD(x\Vert p)\}
\le\exp\{-2n(x-p)^2\}.
\]
The last inequality follows because the second derivative in \(x\) of the binary divergence is \(1/\{x(1-x)\}\ge4\) and the divergence and its first derivative vanish at \(x=p\).  The lower tail is identical.  Inverting at tail probability of order \(n^{-2}\), then taking the union over the fixed number of cells, proves (17).  Hence, with probability tending to one, all laws used by the supremum in \(K_n\) lie in the common saturated neighborhood, where the constraint \(t\in\mathcal T(q)\) is exactly \(t=F(q)\).

Let \(z\) denote reduced observable coordinates and \(\widehat z\) their unrestricted multinomial maximum-likelihood estimate.  A third-order Taylor expansion of each term \(N_j\log z_j\), uniformly on the positive compact neighborhood, gives for \(z-\widehat z=O(n^{-1/2})\)
\[
2\{\ell_n(\widehat z)-\ell_n(z)\}
=n(z-\widehat z)^{\top}\Omega_{\zeta}^{-1}(z-\widehat z)+o_P(1), \tag{18}
\]
uniformly; for two samples the independent blocks and the limit \(n/n_m\to\lambda\) give exactly the displayed \(\Omega_{\zeta}\).  The multinomial central limit theorem cited in \(\mathrm{lem:multinomial\text{-}clt\text{-}and\text{-}delta}\) makes the remainder uniform on bounded local coordinates.

Write \(J=\partial F(\zeta)/\partial\zeta^{\top}\).  Taylor expansion of the common \(F\) gives
\[
F(z)-F(\widehat z)=J(z-\widehat z)+O(\|z-\widehat z\|_2^2). \tag{19}
\]
Strict concavity of the interior multinomial likelihood gives a uniform positive Kullback--Leibler gap outside the fixed saturated neighborhood.  Consequently, for bounded root-\(n\) target displacements, every constrained likelihood maximizer lies in that neighborhood with probability tending to one; no remote atlas component contributes to the local profile.

Minimizing the quadratic form in (18) subject to the linearized constraint in (19) is an explicit Lagrange-multiplier calculation.  Since
\[
V_{\tau}=J\Omega_{\zeta}J^{\top},
\qquad \lambda_{\min}(V_{\tau})\ge\varepsilon,
\]
the multiplier is unique and the minimum equals
\[
n(t-\widehat\tau_n)^{\top}V_{\tau}^{-1}
  (t-\widehat\tau_n)+o_P(1) \tag{20}
\]
uniformly for \(\sqrt n\|t-\widehat\tau_n\|_2\) bounded.  Uniform nonsingularity also shows that targets outside such a bounded local set have profile discrepancy tending uniformly to infinity.  Equations (18)--(20), applied to an independent replicate under every \(q\) in (17), and the uniform finite-alphabet central limit theorem imply
\[
\sup_{q\in C_n:\,t=F(q)}
\left|
P_q\{\Delta_n^{\mathrm{rep}}(t)\ge\Delta_n^{\mathrm{obs}}(t)\}
-\overline F_{\chi^2_2}\!\left(
n(t-\widehat\tau_n)^{\top}\widehat V_n^{-1}
(t-\widehat\tau_n)
\right)
\right|=o_P(1). \tag{21}
\]
uniformly on bounded local target coordinates.  Here covariance consistency follows from the separated-Wald theorem, and the continuous \(\chi^2_2\) law removes lattice ties.  Since \(\beta_n=o(1)\), (21) sandwiches \(K_n\), with probability tending to one, between the ellipsoids obtained by replacing \(\chi^2_{2,1-\alpha}\) by \(\chi^2_{2,1-\alpha}\pm\delta_n\) for some \(\delta_n=o_P(1)\).

The eigenvalues of \(\widehat V_n\) are uniformly bounded above and away from zero with probability tending to one.  Radial comparison of the two sandwiching ellipsoids therefore gives
\[
d_{\mathrm H}(K_n,W_n)\le n^{-1/2}O_P(\delta_n)=o_P(n^{-1/2}).
\]
Local saturation and the positive rank-two target covariance force the local target value into the relative interior, so intersecting both regions with \([0,1]^2\) does not change this comparison.  This proves the claimed compact-uniform Hausdorff limit.  None of steps (17)--(21) is available at a nonsingleton, nonseparated, or nonsaturated profile, so only (16) is asserted there.

theorem.statement:
Yes.  For every fixed finite \((\mathcal W,\mathcal Z)\), there is a one-copy structural compiler \(\mathscr A\) with the following properties.  It first rejects any cell rank exceeding two.  A rank-two cell is represented by its two oriented segment modes, refined by all coefficient support faces.  A rank-one cell is represented by the disjoint \(\mathrm L,\mathrm R,\mathrm E,\mathrm D\) modes of \(\mathrm{lem:rank\text{-}one\text{-}lred\text{-}normal\text{-}forms}\), with the \(\mathrm E\) split refined coordinatewise.  Products of the four local modes use one shared variable \(b_i\) at each response vertex and are refined by proxy supports, endpoint equalities and inequalities, observed-line incidences, and all nonzero pivots.  Their union is exactly \(\mathcal C_A(T)\).  In design B, adjoining \(\rho\), the zero-residual or active negatively proportional state at each response type, lexicographic nonzero pivots, forest propagation, the active-cycle product-one constraint, positive component scales, normalization, and a signed relevance witness gives a finite union equal exactly to \(\mathcal C_B(T)\).

On each nonempty one-copy chart, \(\mathscr A\) computes descriptions and sample points for all semialgebraically connected components before forming the graph \(t=\tau_C\) and projecting it.  On a component with sampled target \(t_0\), it decides and, when possible, samples the refinement \(\tau_C\ne t_0\).  Thus it decides target constancy within every component and compares the exact constants across all components and charts.  It returns incompatibility when the relevant union is empty, an exact common target when all values agree, and otherwise two cycle points with different targets and their legal full-SCM lifts.  The computation uses no generic two-copy unequal-target predicate.  Over an arbitrary real input field \(\mathbb K_{\zeta}\), termination is relative to effective arithmetic, order, sign-determination, and real-root oracles.  A target is reported as a rational expression in \(\mathbb K_{\zeta}\) only when that expression is actually constructed; otherwise it is reported by a real-univariate representation and Thom sign data over \(\mathbb K_{\zeta}\).
theorem.proof_tex:
We prove structural exhaustiveness before invoking any real-algebraic component routine.

First compute the rank of each \(T_e\).  A sum of the two rank-one matrices \(b_ia_{ei}^{\top}\) and \(b_ja_{ej}^{\top}\) has rank at most two, so a rank exceeding two makes the cycle fiber empty.  Rank zero is excluded by selected-table positivity.  Thus only ranks one and two can occur on a nonempty fiber.

Fix a rank-two cell \(e\) with \(\mathcal I_e=\{i,j\}\).  Its normalized columns
\[
c_{ez}=\frac{T_e(\cdot,z)}{v_e(z)}
\]
lie on the observable affine line \(\mathcal L_e\).  In any factorization, \(b_i\ne b_j\), both endpoints lie on \(\mathcal L_e\), and every \(c_{ez}\) lies in the closed segment \([b_i,b_j]\).  Conversely, these segment conditions determine nonnegative coefficients: if \(h_e\) is any coordinate separating the endpoints, then
\[
a_{ei}(z)=v_e(z)
 \frac{c_{ez}(h_e)-b_j(h_e)}{b_i(h_e)-b_j(h_e)},
\qquad
a_{ej}(z)=v_e(z)-a_{ei}(z). \tag{2}
\]
The two possible orders of the endpoints are precisely the two orientations used in \(\mathrm{thm:rank\text{-}two\text{-}orientation\text{-}atlas}\).  Replacing each weak coefficient inequality in (2) by the alternatives zero or strictly positive enumerates every forced-zero face.

For a rank-one cell, \(\mathrm{lem:rank\text{-}one\text{-}lred\text{-}normal\text{-}forms}\) proves that the four displayed modes are disjoint and exhaustive.  Notice in particular that mode \(\mathrm L\) leaves the inactive endpoint \(b_i\) unrestricted except for its simplex and globally shared constraints, and mode \(\mathrm R\) does the analogous thing for \(b_j\).  Hence no unsupported propagation of an inactive endpoint into the observed column span is made.  Mode \(\mathrm E\) retains the whole split vector \(s_e\), which is essential because its coordinates enter the IV residual equations.

Take the product of the local mode lists over the four response-cycle cells.  Use a single normalized variable \(b_i\) for the two occurrences of response type \(i\).  Therefore equality of shared endpoints is imposed, rather than inferred.  Refine each coordinate of each \(b_i\) into zero or positive support, each split or rank-two coefficient into its displayed zero/interior alternatives, and each finite endpoint equality, inequality, line incidence, and pivot into its sign alternatives.  Every refinement is a finite conjunction of polynomial equalities and strict inequalities over \(\mathbb K_{\zeta}\).  Equations (2) and the rank-one normal-form lemma prove that every point of \(\mathcal C_A(T)\) enters at least one refinement.  Direct substitution in each local cell equation proves the reverse inclusion.  Thus the union of these charts is exactly \(\mathcal C_A(T)\), including simultaneous rank-one cells, coincident endpoints, inactive response rows, and forced coefficient zeros.

For design B, fix one of these cycle charts and a positive projective vector \(\rho\).  At each response type, \(\mathrm{thm:iv\text{-}residual\text{-}forest}\) gives an exhaustive alternative: both incident residual vectors vanish, exactly one vanishes and the branch is empty, or both are nonzero and negatively proportional.  In the last case choose the first nonzero coordinate as pivot and refine its sign; this is a finite disjoint pivot list.  Active links determine positive cell-margin ratios.  Since the active graph is a subgraph of the four-cycle, it is either a forest or the whole cycle.  Forest ratios propagate from one positive scale per component, and in the whole-cycle case consistency is equivalent to the single product-one equation.  Positivity of the scales and their normalization give all and only the positive margins.  Finally, enumerate a pair \(z<z'\) and a sign for
\[
q^X_zg(z')-q^X_{z'}g(z)\ne0.
\]
The residual-forest theorem proves that these refinements are necessary and sufficient for \(\mathcal C_B(T)\).  This establishes the claimed structural union before any target test.

Each resulting chart is a one-copy semialgebraic set: its variables are one collection of endpoints, coefficients, and, in design B, projective and margin coordinates.  Clear only denominators whose positivity or nonzero pivot condition is already recorded.  The exact component and roadmap algorithms in \(\mathrm{lem:effective\text{-}real\text{-}algebraic\text{-}components}\) first return a description and a sample point \(x_C\) for every semialgebraically connected component \(C\).  Only after this step form
\[
G_C=\{(x,t):x\in C,\ t=\tau_C(x)\}
\]
and compute its target projection by one-block elimination.  Put \(t_0=\tau_C(x_C)\).  To avoid confusing a positive-dimensional projection with the number of decomposition cells, refine the same component by
\[
\bigl(\tau_{C,1}(x)-t_{0,1}\bigr)^2+
\bigl(\tau_{C,2}(x)-t_{0,2}\bigr)^2>0. \tag{3}
\]
The cited realizability algorithm decides (3).  If it is nonempty, its sampled point \(x_C'\) has a different target.  If it is empty, \(\tau_C\equiv t_0\) on all of \(C\).  This is a one-copy component calculation, not a pair-of-fibers predicate.  Comparing the Thom encodings of the finitely many component constants then decides global agreement across components and overlapping support charts.

The sample value \(t_0\) is represented by a real-univariate encoding over \(\mathbb K_{\zeta}\); adjoining that encoded algebraic element makes every coefficient in (3) effective for the same sign and realizability routines.  Moreover, chart existence, component existence, and target-projection tests eliminate only latent chart coordinates, so their final signs and Thom comparisons depend only on the observed input \(\zeta\).  They are therefore observable tests.

When all constants agree, a sampled target coordinate is already an exact output.  If field arithmetic has constructed it as a rational expression in \(\mathbb K_{\zeta}\), the compiler returns that expression.  Otherwise the sampling and elimination algorithms return a real-univariate representation with Thom data, and the compiler retains that encoding even if an unperformed simplification could place the number back in \(\mathbb K_{\zeta}\).  If agreement fails, either (3) supplies two points in one component or two constant components supply one sampled point each.  The previously proved structural union makes both legal cycle points.  The cycle-to-SCM lift then gives two full SCMs with the same observables and, in design A, the same supplied margins.  This proves every asserted output and completes the open-ended question.

added_lemmas.statement:
Let \(e\in\mathcal E\) have \(\mathcal I_e=\{i,j\}\), and suppose that \(T_e\) has rank one.  There is then a unique \(c_e\in\Delta_{\mathcal W}^{\circ}\) such that \(T_e=c_ev_e^{\top}\).  Every nonnegative factorization of this cell in \(\mathcal C_A(T)\) belongs to exactly one of the following four modes:
\[
\begin{array}{ll}
\mathrm L:& b_i\ne c_e,\quad b_j=c_e,\quad a_{ei}\equiv0,\quad a_{ej}=v_e,\\
\mathrm R:& b_i=c_e,\quad b_j\ne c_e,\quad a_{ei}=v_e,\quad a_{ej}\equiv0,\\
\mathrm E:& b_i=b_j=c_e,\quad a_{ei}=s_e,\quad a_{ej}=v_e-s_e,
             \quad 0\le s_e(z)\le v_e(z),\\
\mathrm D:& b_i\ne b_j,\quad 0<q_e<1,\quad
             c_e=q_eb_i+(1-q_e)b_j,\quad
             a_{ei}=q_ev_e,\quad a_{ej}=(1-q_e)v_e.
\end{array}
\]
In mode \(\mathrm E\), the coordinatewise alternatives \(s_e(z)=0\), \(0<s_e(z)<v_e(z)\), and \(s_e(z)=v_e(z)\) give an exhaustive finite support-face refinement.
added_lemmas.proof_tex:
Selected-table positivity gives \(T_e(w,z)>0\) and hence
\[
v_e(z)=\sum_{w\in\mathcal W}T_e(w,z)>0
\]
for every \(z\in\mathcal Z\).  Since \(T_e\) has rank one, all of its nonzero columns are proportional.  Normalizing each column by its positive sum therefore gives one common vector
\[
c_e=\frac{T_e(\cdot,z)}{v_e(z)}\in\Delta_{\mathcal W}^{\circ},
\qquad T_e=c_ev_e^{\top}.
\]
For a factorization in \(\mathcal C_A(T)\), put
\[
q_z=\frac{a_{ei}(z)}{v_e(z)}\in[0,1].
\]
The cell equation and \(a_{ei}(z)+a_{ej}(z)=v_e(z)\) yield, after division by the positive number \(v_e(z)\),
\[
c_e=q_zb_i+(1-q_z)b_j. \tag{1}
\]
If \(b_i=b_j\), equation (1) and normalization imply \(b_i=b_j=c_e\); the vector \(s_e=a_{ei}\) is otherwise arbitrary subject exactly to \(0\le s_e\le v_e\).  This is mode \(\mathrm E\).

Suppose instead that \(b_i\ne b_j\).  Choose \(w_\star\) with \(b_i(w_\star)\ne b_j(w_\star)\).  The \(w_\star\)-coordinate of (1) gives
\[
q_z=\frac{c_e(w_\star)-b_j(w_\star)}{b_i(w_\star)-b_j(w_\star)},
\]
which is independent of \(z\).  Denote it by \(q_e\).  If \(q_e=0\), equation (1) gives \(b_j=c_e\), and the inequalities \(b_i\ne b_j\) and \(a_{ei}=0\), \(a_{ej}=v_e\) give mode \(\mathrm L\).  The case \(q_e=1\) is mode \(\mathrm R\).  The remaining case \(0<q_e<1\) is mode \(\mathrm D\).  These cases are disjoint by their displayed equality and inequality conditions.  Conversely, direct substitution shows that every point in any displayed mode satisfies the cell equation and coefficient normalization.  Finally, for each of the finitely many \(z\), exactly one of \(s_e(z)=0\), \(0<s_e(z)<v_e(z)\), and \(s_e(z)=v_e(z)\) holds.  Their products over \(z\) are therefore a finite exhaustive refinement of mode \(\mathrm E\).

added_lemmas.statement: Suppose a cycle point in design A has \(m\in\Delta_{\mathcal E}^{\circ}\), \(b_i(w)>0\) for all \((i,w)\), and \(a_{ei}(z)>0\) for every incident \((e,i,z)\).  Suppose a cycle point in design B satisfies the analogous strict inequalities, including the defining positivity of \(m\) and \(g\).  Then its full-SCM lift may be chosen with every response mass, proxy and instrument kernel, treatment probability, and selection probability strictly between its relevant boundary values.  Consequently, two target-changing cycle witnesses that both lie in interior support charts have strictly positive full-SCM lifts.
added_lemmas.proof_tex:
Consider design A first.  For every response type \(i\), define
\[
h_i(z)=\sum_{e:\,i\in\mathcal I_e}m_ea_{ei}(z),
\qquad
\pi_i=\sum_{z\in\mathcal Z}h_i(z).
\]
The strict positivity of \(m_e\) and of every incident coefficient gives \(h_i(z)>0\) and \(\pi_i>0\).  Hence
\[
g_i(z)=\frac{h_i(z)}{\pi_i}>0
\]
is a normalized instrument kernel.  Let \(e_1(i)\) and \(e_0(i)\) be the two incident cells of type \(i\) having treatment coordinates one and zero.  Define
\[
e_i(z)=\frac{m_{e_1(i)}a_{e_1(i),i}(z)}{h_i(z)}.
\]
Both the numerator and the omitted term \(m_{e_0(i)}a_{e_0(i),i}(z)\) are positive, so \(0<e_i(z)<1\).  The given \(b_i(w)\) are strictly positive.  Since \(p\) is positive, \(r_e>0\).  Choose
\[
c_0=\frac12\min_{e\in\mathcal E}\frac{m_e}{r_e}>0,
\qquad
s_e=\frac{c_0r_e}{m_e}.
\]
Then \(0<s_e\le1/2<1\), and
\[
\sum_e s_em_e=c_0\sum_er_e=c_0.
\]
The direct lift calculation in \(\mathrm{lem:cycle\text{-}to\text{-}scm\text{-}lift}\) now gives the required selected law and target, while the displayed inequalities prove strict positivity of every stochastic mechanism.

In design B, the shared-instrument equations give
\[
h_i(z)=\sum_{e:\,i\in\mathcal I_e}m_ea_{ei}(z)=\pi_i g(z).
\]
The left side is strictly positive, and \(g(z)>0\), so \(\pi_i>0\).  The same treatment-probability formula has a positive numerator and positive complementary incident contribution and is therefore in \((0,1)\).  The same choice of \(c_0\) makes every selection probability lie in \((0,1)\).  Thus the IV lift is also strictly positive.  Applying the construction separately to two interior cycle witnesses proves the final assertion.

added_lemmas.statement:
For a positive selected table \(p\), the design-A full fiber is nonempty if and only if
\[
m\in\Delta_{\mathcal E}^{\circ}
\quad\text{and}\quad
\mathcal C_A(T)\ne\varnothing.
\]
Thus strict positivity of the supplied margin is an observable compatibility test and not an additional maintained assumption.
added_lemmas.proof_tex: If \(\mathcal F_A(p,m)\ne\varnothing\), \(\mathrm{lem:compatible\text{-}margin\text{-}positivity}\) gives \(m\in\Delta_{\mathcal E}^{\circ}\), and the forward map in \(\mathrm{lem:cycle\text{-}to\text{-}scm\text{-}lift}\) gives a point of \(\mathcal C_A(T)\).  This proves necessity.  Conversely, suppose \(m\in\Delta_{\mathcal E}^{\circ}\) and choose \((b,a)\in\mathcal C_A(T)\).  The converse construction in \(\mathrm{lem:cycle\text{-}to\text{-}scm\text{-}lift}\), with the positive supplied margin \(m\), produces a legal \(\vartheta\in\mathcal F_A(p,m)\).  Hence the two displayed conditions are sufficient.

added_lemmas.statement: Let \(D\) be an effective ordered domain and let a semialgebraic subset of a real closed extension of the fraction field of \(D\) be given by a Boolean formula in finitely many polynomial sign conditions.  There are exact algorithms that compute roadmaps and sample points meeting every semialgebraically connected component, decide realizability after adjoining further polynomial sign conditions, eliminate one block of variables, and encode sampled real algebraic coordinates by real-univariate representations with Thom data.  Their numbers of arithmetic operations, output degrees, and, for integer input, coefficient bit sizes are bounded by explicit computable functions of the number of variables, the number and degrees of the input polynomials, and the input coefficient bit size.

added_lemmas.statement: For independent identically distributed finite-dimensional random vectors with finite second moments, the normalized sample mean satisfies the multivariate central limit theorem.  If a map is differentiable at the population mean, the delta method maps that limit through its derivative.  Slutsky's lemma and the continuous-mapping theorem preserve these limits under consistent plug-in transformations.  The same conclusions hold jointly for independent samples after deterministic relative-rate rescaling.

proposed_statement_changes.proposed:
For design A, \(\mathscr A\) first tests \(m\in\Delta_{\mathcal E}^{\circ}\) and \(\mathcal C_A(T)\ne\varnothing\).  If either test fails, \(\mathcal F_A(p,m)=\varnothing\) and the law is not rigid under \(\lvert\mathcal T_A(p,m)\rvert=1\).  Otherwise \(\lvert\mathcal T_A(p,m)\rvert=1\) if and only if the finite observable rank, support, incidence, component, and cycle agreement tests returned by \(\mathscr A(T,m)\) hold.  For design B, \(\mathscr A\) first tests \(\mathcal C_B(T)\ne\varnothing\); failure means an empty, hence non-rigid, full fiber, and otherwise \(\lvert\mathcal T_B(p)\rvert=1\) if and only if the corresponding residual-forest, component, and cycle agreement tests returned by \(\mathscr A(T)\) hold.

For an arbitrary real input \(\zeta\), a rigid value is returned as a rational expression in \(\mathbb K_{\zeta}\) only when the compiler constructs such an expression; every other value is returned as a uniquely ordered real element of a finite algebraic extension, encoded by a square-free real-univariate polynomial over \(\mathbb K_{\zeta}\), rational coordinate functions, and Thom sign data.  For explicitly rational \(\zeta\), the encoding may be normalized to a square-free integer polynomial and rational isolating interval.  Every nonrigid output contains two legal full SCMs with identical observables and supplied margins when supplied, but different \(\tau\).  If both selected cycle witnesses lie in interior support charts, their full-SCM lifts can be chosen strictly positive; no strict-positivity claim is made for a witness lying on a boundary face.
proposed_statement_changes.reason: The current wording does not classify empty fibers and overstates when a field-rational representation or strictly positive twins are returned. The replacement preserves the rigidity result while making compatibility, output representation, and the interior-witness condition exact.

proposed_statement_changes.proposed: On every observable law in the regular domain of Conditions 2--3 of Shingaki--Yoshida--Kuroki (2026) for which the corresponding Condition-1 full SCM fiber is nonempty, the fiber is rigid and the value returned by \(\mathscr A\) equals the PN/PS value obtained from Appendix equations (A.28)--(A.33). proposed_statement_changes.reason: The published formula applies to compatible Condition-1 laws, and an incompatible boundary table cannot receive either a rigidity or twin certificate. The replacement adds precisely those compatibility qualifications and preserves the regular-domain and boundary conclusions.

proposed_statement_changes.proposed:
Fix \(k=\lvert\mathcal Z\rvert\) and \(\ell=\lvert\mathcal W\rvert\).  Before endpoint-incidence sign subdivision and connected-component subdivision, the number of structural mode products used by \(\mathscr A\) is at most
\[
N^{\mathrm{str}}_{A,k,\ell}
=(2^{\ell}-1)^4(3^{k+1}+3)^4
\]
in design A and at most
\[
N^{\mathrm{str}}_{B,k,\ell}
=N^{\mathrm{str}}_{A,k,\ell}(2k-1)^4k(k-1)
\]
in design B.  The compiler terminates over an arbitrary \(\mathbb K_{\zeta}\) relative to effective arithmetic, order, sign-determination, and real-root oracles.

Let \(B_{k,\ell}\) be the computable maximum of the two displayed structural counts and the explicit component-count and output-degree bounds obtained by instantiating the roadmap, sampling, real-root, and one-block-elimination algorithms of Basu--Pollack--Roy with
\[
N=4\ell+10k+12,
\qquad
s=100(k\ell+k^2+\ell+1),
\qquad d=4.
\]
Then \(B_{k,\ell}\) bounds the total number of labeled component outputs and every algebraic degree over \(\mathbb K_{\zeta}\); in particular, for a universal computable constant \(C\),
\[
B_{k,\ell}\le 2^{,2^{C(k\ell+k+\ell+1)}}.
\]
For rational input coordinates of binary length at most \(L\), let \(H_{k,\ell}(L)\) be the corresponding computable maximum of the published integer-coefficient and real-root-isolation bit bounds after denominator clearing.  A Turing implementation terminates, and every integer polynomial coefficient and rational isolating endpoint in an output certificate has binary length at most \(H_{k,\ell}(L)\).  No smaller closed-form height bound is asserted.  The classification uses the exhaustive structural charts followed by one-copy component calculations, not a generic two-copy quantifier-elimination classifier.
proposed_statement_changes.reason: The former height formula did not identify the published effective bound from which it followed. The replacement gives the corrected structural-mode product, oracle-relative computation for arbitrary real coefficient fields, and computable bounds obtained by explicit instantiation of the cited algorithms.

proposed_statement_changes.proposed:
For the Clopper--Pearson preliminary region \(C_n\), profile discrepancy \(\Delta_n\), and Berger--Boos calibration in \(\operatorname{pv}_n\),
\[
P_{\vartheta}\{\tau(\vartheta)\in K_n\}\ge1-\alpha
\]
at every sample size for every \(\vartheta\) in either design.  This bound holds along arbitrary sequences approaching \(\mathfrak D\), including point-to-set transitions.

The following additional Hausdorff conclusion is restricted to locally saturated separated rigid profiles.  Uniformly over any compact subset of \(\mathfrak R_{\varepsilon}\) for which there are a fixed neighborhood radius and one twice continuously differentiable map \(F\) such that every observable law \(q\) in that neighborhood is compatible, its identified set is \(\mathcal T_A(q)=\{F(q)\}\) in design A or \(\mathcal T_B(q)=\{F(q)\}\) in design B, and every incident chart continuation equals \(F\),
\[

\]

proposed_statement_changes.reason: Exact coverage is unchanged. The optional Hausdorff comparison requires a locally saturated compatible observable neighborhood; without it an exact rank-constrained fiber can have no regular off-model profile despite a smooth chart extension.

prose_updates.tldr: For every fixed finite four-response-type selected proxy model, a boundary-complete structural atlas now decides PN/PS target rigidity. It exhausts rank-two orientations and the four disjoint rank-one modes, retains equal-endpoint split vectors and inactive rows, and adds response-level residual forests for the unknown-margin relevant-IV design. A one-copy real-algebraic component evaluator returns an exact common target, two legal same-observable SCMs, or model incompatibility. Arbitrary real inputs are handled relative to coefficient-field arithmetic and sign oracles; rational expressions are promised only when constructed, with real-univariate and Thom encodings otherwise. Exact confidence-fiber coverage remains universal, while Wald and Hausdorff equivalence are confined to separated, locally saturated rigid profiles.

project_justification.gap: Published regular proxy formulas do not classify PN/PS constancy when ranks fall, coefficients reach support faces, endpoints coincide, response rows become inactive, or shared-instrument equations couple unknown population margins. General real-algebraic decidability alone also does not expose the causal response-cycle obstruction.
project_justification.niche: The four response types form a labeled cycle whose causal target may be rigid even while nuisance factorizations vary. Exhaustive local edge modes, shared endpoints, and residual forests reduce every legal fiber to finitely many one-copy component problems without replacing the causal classification by a two-copy unequal-target predicate.
project_justification.fill: The completed compiler gives necessary and sufficient compatibility and target-agreement tests for both supplied-margin and relevant-IV designs. It computes connected components before target projection, tests a sampled component against a different target value, and returns exact algebraic values or legal full-SCM twins. The statistical layer combines separated-chart Wald inference with universal finite-sample confidence-fiber coverage.

sampling_model.overlap: All population selected cells are positive. A nonempty supplied-margin fiber forces every population cell margin to be positive. Wald inference additionally requires separated incident charts, common first derivatives, smooth local continuations, and target covariance bounded away from singularity; Hausdorff equivalence of profile and Wald regions also requires a locally saturated compatible observable neighborhood.
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: Reduced selected-table and independent margin coordinates use empirical multinomial frequencies and the block-diagonal plug-in covariance. The deterministic chart selector uses the stated tolerance and full-square fallback. Transition inference profiles the exact multinomial discrepancy over the complete compatible target fiber and applies Berger--Boos calibration; this gives finite-sample coverage even when chart selection or point identification fails.

prose_updates.related_work: Shingaki, Yoshida, and Kuroki (2026) provide the selected response-type model and regular PN/PS inversion formulas; the compatibility-qualified anchor theorem proves agreement on that regular domain and extends classification, not their formula, to singular and boundary fibers. Shingaki and Kuroki (2023) identify response-type probabilities in a randomized no-selection proxy experiment, and Kawakami (2021) identifies the corresponding IV-plus-proxy quantities under its stated invertibility and separation conditions. The atlas agrees on those overlaps and separately classifies an explicit selected boundary datum outside Kawakami's invertibility domain, without a subsumption claim. Nonnegative-factorization rigidity work supplies useful geometry but does not state causal target constancy on this labeled cycle. Basu, Pollack, and Roy (2006) supply the classical one-copy roadmap, connected-component, real-root, and elimination algorithms used only after the causal L/R/E/D and residual-forest atlas has been proved exhaustive.
prose_updates.technical_internal_limitation: The exact compiler is a theorem-level symbolic procedure, not a claim of a completed production implementation or favorable variable-alphabet complexity. Over arbitrary real observables, computation is relative to effective arithmetic, order, sign, and real-root oracles. A rational field expression is returned only when constructed; otherwise the exact output remains a real-univariate and Thom encoding. Strictly positive twins are guaranteed only when both chosen cycle witnesses are on interior support charts. Universal confidence coverage does not imply shrinking at a nonidentified transition, and first-order Hausdorff agreement requires a locally saturated separated rigid profile. The frozen materials still lack the released numerical GEUVADIS count table and binarization thresholds, so no empirical compatibility or rigidity verdict for that dataset is claimed here.
prose_updates.honest_scope: The mathematical contribution is the exhaustive fixed-alphabet structural response-cycle classifier plus exact one-copy component evaluation. Empty fibers are reported as incompatibility and are non-rigid under the cardinality-one definition. The field-relative and rational-input output tiers are distinct. Regular overlap results are agreement checks, and the Kawakami boundary example is a one-law scope separation only. Wald inference requires chart separation, common first derivatives, smooth continuations, proportional margin sampling when applicable, and nonsingular target covariance. Exact confidence-fiber coverage holds without those conditions; its optional Wald-equivalence clause additionally requires a locally saturated compatible neighborhood. The GEUVADIS application remains an audit protocol conditional on the graph and on recovery of the actual released table, not a new numerical reanalysis.
